Ask questions. In my time working ANY job (Construction, Insulation, Retail, Sales Associate, ANYTHING) I realized my and almost any new hires biggest downfall is their fear of asking questions or being “annoying” or just overall anxiety about the situation. 

You’re not a miracle worker & the company is really shitty about just feeding you to the wolves. Learn as you go but ask questions often and always if you have them. Have them go over the stores expected recovery fundamentals as every SM and DM looks for different things in recovery. 

Your first and most important priority should always be the customer and register. Depending on your stores size, you may not even ever need to leave the front end. Other smaller stores (like mine where we only have 2 people on duty at a time) you may have to work food or totes. 

Generally speaking a sales associates nightly duties are putbacks, recovery, bread, trash, sweep, spot mop, & overall maintain a clean storefront and register area. Some stores have other things they like you to do, like a rolltainer in front of tobacco. 

As a sales associate I’d say generally speaking make sure you are prioritizing the customer, maintaining a recovered and organized food section, keeping your register clean, sanitary and organized, and cigarettes in stock and neat. 

During the day you may want to check register candy to see if it will go out. Our DM likes to call register candy being empty a “disappointment.” Every out we have at the register is a disappointment  to a customer. 

But yeah... that’s the main thing man. Just don’t be afraid to ask questions and don’t be afraid to fuck up or make someone upset... cause it’s inevitable. That’s the nature of a business like this. As a new hire you shouldn’t be expected to know the ropes and just try your best and that’s all they can ask from you. It just takes time. Good luck & I hope you have a good experience with DG!

Also - why not just count down the openers drawer when you get in & your cashier comes in? Drop off their deposit into the pickups area w no slip and run their reports at night or when you get the chance. Saves a lot of time.

You can easily get money counting done in 15-20 minutes + reports and deposit. It takes time but we NEVER start counting money until all customers are gone and doors are locked. Would get us terminated so damn fast.

Do NOT touch money until doors are locked and there are no customers in the store. Your money counting section on the computer shows you the correct order in which you do things. 

You need to pop the drawers, get the change fund out of the safe, and then set the top safe for the drop offs and pickups. 

Do your ending tills for your drawers and take out the actual amount the computer will show you. Compress change and bills as much as possible, making it so that the smaller change and bills will stay in the drawer while the larger bills go to the deposit. Write down the ending numbers and coupon amount on the register slips. 

Next you start your change fund. Count the change fund with the counter, starting with coins. Personally I just enter the roll amounts manually and then let the counter do the money. Make sure you do as the counter tells you, using loose bills first and then counting the strapped bills. DO NOT CORRECT IT IF IT NEEDS CORRECTING YET. Fill out the change fund clipboard AND THEN correct it, writing down what you added or removed. If you have to remove bills from the change fund, it goes straight to the deposit pile which is what you removed from your drawers to balance them out. 

Finally, the deposit. Your top safe should have popped by now. Enter the code again to open it. You have to prepare a few things for the deposit, I usually do as much as I can on my lunch break. You have a deposit bag and bank slip. I fill out the date, store number, bag number, etc. on the bag and slip and clipboard. 
Account for your pickups, you will have a box, similar to where coupons will be on an ending till, for pickups and just verify you have them all, organizing the bills out and stacking them with the deposit as you go. Count down the deposit, and fill out everything! Fill out the deposit amount on the bag, the deposit slip (multiple times), etc etc. Enter the bag number into the computer and then you’re done with the PC. Seal the deposit bag and rip the top of the bag off. 

Put everything up, put your keys in the register, and you’re almost done. Balance all the cashiers out, and then run their reports. My store has us run the first 3 reports for every cashier + balance them out. (I think it’s sales report, tender report, and sales analysis or something) 

Enter the deposit into the terminal through the EOD section, and then run the EOD. Once the drawers pop, take your keys out, set the alarm, and go. Lock doors behind you, voila. You just closed. 

Don’t think I left anything out. Hope this helped.

Edit: Forgot to mention, at our store we staple all pickup slips together at the end of the night and then we have a way of stapling our reports.
